purpose: Current machine-readable feature manual for GPT/API calls that convert informal Korean MathGraph drawing requests into validated GraphA operations.

defaultStylePolicy.colorFieldGuidance: Omit color and fillColor unless the user explicitly requests a non-black color; when included by default, use #000000.
defaultStylePolicy.explicitColorSupport: Specific user-requested colors remain supported through color and fillColor.

sourceOfTruth.importantRule: This manual describes the current local runtime. If SchemaValidator, PatchApplier, AIService, or ObjectManager changes, update this file and the synthetic examples together.

defaultFlow: Classify the Korean request into tags such as plane, circle, solid, graph, number_line, or chart_approximation.
Read retrieval-index.json and load only matching manual chunks and examples.
If the request is a full math problem, extract diagram-relevant conditions and draw a supporting graph/diagram instead of solving the problem.
Plan dependency order: support points first, base primitives second, derived construction objects third, markers/dimensions/styles last.
Return only valid JSON when the caller needs a MathGraph patch.

responsesApiNotes.recommendedContract: Use the existing strict Structured Outputs schema named graph_operations from AIService.js.
responsesApiNotes.statePolicy: Use current canvas objects as compact context with id, type, label, coordinates, expressions, number-line fields, and dependencies.
responsesApiNotes.tokenPolicy: Keep stable reusable instructions and selected schema chunks before request-specific prompt text. Do not include the full synthetic dataset unless retrieval selects it.
responsesApiNotes.storagePolicy: Current local OpenAI path sets store: false.
responsesApiNotes.runtimeReferenceLoading: AIService tries to fetch retrieval-index.json and feature-manual.json in browser API calls, selects relevant object types from the prompt/context, and injects a compact manual summary before the request-specific instruction.
responsesApiNotes.problemSituationMode: Long textbook-style problem text routes to internal problem_diagram mode. The model should not solve, answer, copy prose, or copy choices; it should extract axes, functions, equations, inequalities, number lines, plane/solid geometry, tangencies, intersections, markers, and shaded regions useful for an editable black-and-white exam diagram.
responsesApiNotes.fullPhotoRecreateMode: Image-only upload/paste treats a whole photo as recreate mode. The model should first reconstruct a visible math diagram/graph/figure. If no printed diagram is visible but the problem prose explicitly describes drawable geometry, it should use that prose as semantic input to construct an editable exam-style supporting diagram without copying the prose, solving the problem, or inventing conditions.
responsesApiNotes.imagePreprocessing: Before OpenAI image analysis, the browser trims only safe background-like margins and downscales oversized images to a readable long-edge budget. Small or already readable images are not shrunk, and suspicious tiny crops are rejected.
responsesApiNotes.imageModelRouting: OpenAI image analysis uses gpt-5.4-mini for the first attempt, then escalates repair to the configured stronger model or gpt-5.5 when semantic intent validation rejects the first GraphA payload.
responsesApiNotes.modelDisclosure: Successful AI drawing result messages show a small chat metadata line with the model that produced the accepted patch, including first -> final model routing when repair escalation happened.
responsesApiNotes.imagePatchRepair: OpenAI image analysis retries once when semantic intent validation rejects the first GraphA payload.

apiPrompting.toolSearchPattern: For future API orchestration with many tool/function schemas, defer rarely used tool definitions and use tool_search or an app-owned retrieval step to load only relevant MathGraph schema chunks.

visualGuardrails: Problem diagram mode must create the exam figure only: no solution text, no copied body prose, no copied answer choices, and no long explanatory labels.
Problem diagram mode defaults to monochrome exam style: thin black strokes, sparse hatching/light shading, concise labels, and hidden helper points with visible:false or pointSize:0.
For construction-only polygons that should look like outlines, set fillOpacity:0; omit positive fill unless a shaded region is requested.
For two-circle lens overlaps, use lensRegion with circle1Id and circle2Id instead of polygon approximations.
For angleDimension, point1Id and point2Id must be distinct from vertexId and far enough from the vertex to render a visible non-degenerate arc.

When a right-angle mark sits on a crowded point or radial center, add a larger angleDimension with arcRadius at least 0.7 and showValue:false instead of relying only on the default small rightAngleMarker.

Use labelOffset on required labels near tangency points, angle markers, collinear construction points, or crowded intersections; hiding helper labels is not enough when requested labels remain close to geometry.

For focus/directrix, tangent-from-point, feasible-region, and named construction-point prompts, create the named points at the exact requested coordinates and create reference lines from support points on the exact equation.
For concentric circles and fixed-radius tangency diagrams, reuse the same center id and place radius points at the requested numeric distance.
For annular-sector-like requests, current GraphA has no first-class annularSector. Use a normal sector plus inner circle outline only when approximation is acceptable.
For function-bounded curved fills, approximate with a polygon through explicit boundary/sample points and hide helper vertices unless a future first-class region exists.

For whole-problem text prompts, do not create objects for the full problem prose or answer choices; create only the graph, figure, labels, functions, and shaded regions needed to visualize the situation.

For full-photo recreation, prioritize a visible diagram and preserve relative positions of axes, ticks, labels, intersections, tangencies, solid/dashed strokes, and shaded regions. If no diagram is printed, extract only explicit drawable relations from the problem text and construct the supporting diagram without solving it.

GraphA point x/y values are math coordinates, not screen pixels. For image reconstruction without explicit coordinate values, keep every point within +/-20 math units so the diagram remains visible in the default canvas view.
For coordinate graph photos, use function objects for smooth visible graphs and preserve short equation labels; use vector objects for standalone direction arrows.

For solid prompts, make the outer prism/pyramid projection large enough to read; cross-section polygons should span a substantial middle portion of the outer solid instead of becoming a tiny internal square.

For nested solids, use prism/pyramid objects, keep inner solid vertices inside the outer projection, leave visible margins from the outer edges, and keep projected centers visually separated instead of piling them on the same screen area.
For pyramids, apexId must not appear in baseVertexIds and should be a real apex separated from the base centroid.
Hide construction helper points with visible:false when they are only used to shape regions or guide construction.

runtimeQualityEnhancement.pipelinePosition: After AI JSON parsing and before command results are returned or recreate-mode image results are semantically accepted.
rules: Add screen-space labelOffset values for crowded visible point labels, tangent labels such as T1/T2, and Euler-line labels O/G/H.
Add a larger hidden-label angleDimension aid for right-angle requests when a rightAngleMarker alone may be visually weak.
Expand prism cross-section prompts so the outer projection is broad and the section polygon spans a substantial middle portion.
Expand and recenter triangular-pyramid-inside-triangular-prism prompts so the inner solid has visible projection margins.

sceneGraphPipeline.purpose: Root architecture for image/PDF recreation: ask the model for a high-level math scene, then compile it deterministically into GraphA operations.

sceneRootShape.nodes: Array of math entities such as point, segment, vector, circle, ellipse, hyperbola, parabola, arc, sector, lensRegion, polygon, function, numberLine, textLabel, prism, pyramid, cylinder, cone, sphere.
sceneRootShape.relations: Array of constraints or annotations such as intersection, midpoint, parallel, perpendicular, rightAngle, equalLength, angleDimension, lengthDimension, tangentFunction.
sceneRootShape.unsupported: Array of unsupported first-class requests such as native statistical charts, tables, nets, annular sectors, or exact function-bounded curved fills.
sceneRootShape.notes: Optional source evidence, uncertainty, or crop notes.

compiler.rule: The compiler creates support points first, then base primitives, then relation/annotation objects.
compiler.warningPolicy: Unsupported scene nodes must become warnings, not guessed invalid GraphA operations.

sceneGraphPipeline.promptingRule: For image/PDF recreate mode, the model should preserve visible mathematical structure and relations in the scene graph. It should not directly invent low-level GraphA operations when a scene graph path is available.

createRules: id is optional but strongly recommended for references inside the same payload.
Referenced objects must already exist on the canvas or be created earlier in the operations array.
updateRules: Only supported mutable fields are applied by PatchApplier.
Position update with x/y applies to point-like objects with position.
deleteRules: Dependent objects are cascade-deleted by ObjectManager.

strictStructuredOutputs.nullableFields: The OpenAI strict schema represents optional fields as nullable and then stripNullFields removes nulls before local validation.

createAndUpdate.name: id
createAndUpdate.note: Stable temporary ID for within-batch references or existing ID for mutation.

createAndUpdate.name: label
createAndUpdate.note: Human-readable label such as A, B, f, c.

createAndUpdate.name: color
createAndUpdate.note: Stroke or primary object color. Default output is #000000; omit unless explicitly needed.

createAndUpdate.name: visible
createAndUpdate.note: Whether object renders and can be selected without show-hidden mode.

createAndUpdate.name: fillColor
createAndUpdate.note: Area fill color for circle, polygon, sector, circularSegment, and lensRegion. Default fill is #000000 with opacity.

createAndUpdate.name: labelOffset
createAndUpdate.note: Screen-space label offset for objects that support labels.

aiPanelFeatures.textCommand: Korean natural language or direct JSON can be submitted through the chat panel.
aiPanelFeatures.directJson: Messages beginning with {, [, or code fences are parsed directly as GraphA operations.
aiPanelFeatures.imageAnalysis: Image upload sends a vision request when API key/provider support is configured.
aiPanelFeatures.configStorage: Provider, API key, model, reasoning effort, and verbosity are stored in localStorage.
aiPanelFeatures.supportPreflight: Before generation, classify requests as supported, approximated, excluded, or unknown. Keep the original prompt on warning/error and expose retry after generation failure.

teacherWorkflow.layout: Canvas-first workspace with a persistent bottom AI command dock and right-side exam-quality summary.
teacherWorkflow.projectFiles: Named versioned mathgraph-project JSON envelopes preserve view and editable objects for later revision.
teacherWorkflow.qualitySummary: Reports object count and support status before and after generation.

exportAndPersistence.projectFile: Exports and imports a named versioned mathgraph-project JSON envelope with view and editable objects.
exportAndPersistence.projectImportValidation: Rejects unknown format/version, invalid view data, and non-array object collections before replacing the current project.
exportAndPersistence.localSave: Saves canvas offset, scale, and ObjectManager JSON to localStorage key graphA_save.
exportAndPersistence.localLoad: Loads saved object graph and clears history baseline.

validationWorkflow: Validate operation and required fields with SchemaValidator.
Validate references against existing IDs plus earlier create IDs.
Validate intent constraints for image patch/recreate workflows, including selected-object mutation and recreate operation budget.
Rollback object/history/selection state if any operation fails.
Render and update sidebar after success.

knownGapsAndApproximations.gap: Statistical chart primitives are not first-class objects.
knownGapsAndApproximations.currentApproximation: The standard teacher generation workflow explicitly excludes bar/pie charts, histograms, frequency polygons, box plots, dot plots, and scatter plots instead of claiming first-class support.

knownGapsAndApproximations.gap: Two-valued intersections support branch 0 or 1, but do not expose semantic left/right/upper/lower anchor names.
knownGapsAndApproximations.currentApproximation: Use branch 0 or 1 after checking object order, or create explicit support points when a semantic side name must remain stable.

knownGapsAndApproximations.gap: Ellipse, hyperbola, and parabola are first-class drawable objects, but automatic conic intersections, point-on-conic constraints, and conic tangents are not first-class yet.
knownGapsAndApproximations.currentApproximation: Create explicitly calculated free points and ordinary lines when their numeric coordinates are known; do not claim that those helpers stay constrained after conic parameter edits.

knownGapsAndApproximations.gap: Annular sectors and exact function-bounded curved regions are not first-class objects.
knownGapsAndApproximations.currentApproximation: Use sectors, circles, polygons, and hidden helper points only when approximation is acceptable. State that exact ring-sector cutouts or exact fill-between-functions need future primitives.
